startup.name: Calltree
startup.one_liner: Enterprise-grade AI support reps for call centers
startup.description: Calltree makes AI support reps for call centers that take voice calls and chats and can also use internal enterprise tools such as a homegrown CRM or internal dashboards, like trained human agents. Buyers are call center operators and enterprises, paid per usage or seat. Team of 14 in San Francisco, Winter 2025 batch.

yc_acceptance.basis: Already in the batch, so this is reported for completeness only. Start from the roughly 1 percent prior for a random applicant in references/yc_acceptance.md (band 0.6 to 2 percent), then adjust: a painful, paid problem and AI voice interest at YC lift it about 2x, a team of 14 helps, and a very crowded voice agent category takes some back; no traction is stated.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say no because voice support agents were the most crowded AI category in late 2024, with several YC companies already in it, and the input offers no customers, revenue or proof that its internal tool use beats peers. The acceptance estimate is a prior for a random applicant and does not rank this company, and since it is already in the batch it matters only as context for the ladder.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2024 --industry B2B: seed 47% / 53% / 59%, cond 53% (n=878). Timing: months_to_seed p25 4, p50 8, p75 20 (n=468). Tag Customer Service has only 9 companies (seed 89%), too few to use.
anchors.adjustment_reason: The anchor of 0.53 is the ever reached figure. The window is 22 months, which covers roughly 78 percent of B2B seed raises by timing, giving about 0.41. I do not lift for the hot voice AI theme, per the winners test rule, and this number does not rank Calltree against other companies.

bands.rationale: Small post YC round of $1M to $3M from angels and micro funds, the YC deal alone (about $500K) is excluded by the seed definition. Voice AI funding grew sharply in 2024, which raises the chance of a larger round for teams with enterprise pilots.
Institutional seed of $3M to $6M, near the 2022 and later median of $3.5M in round_benchmarks.csv, which includes the YC deal and reads low, so this band carries the most weight.
Larger institutional seed where press covered 2026 raises had a median of $6.0M (quartiles $4.3M and $10M, n=77, press leans to big rounds); needs live revenue or a standout team story.
Upside seed above $12M, seen in 2025 AI categories when several funds bid for a team with early enterprise traction.

ladder.why_it_fails: Voice and support AI was extremely crowded by January 2025, with Vapi and Synthflow already past a Series A and YC peers Bland AI (S23), Retell AI (W24) and Giga (S23) in the same field, so investors will ask why a 14 person team wins enterprise call centers. The pitch of using internal tools is a real wedge but proof will need named enterprise logos and call volumes, and many peers claimed the same in decks.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2024 --industry B2B: series_a cond 26% (n=468), ever 14% known-only. Timing: months_to_series_a p25 21, median 28, p75 37 (n=123).
anchors.adjustment_reason: The anchor is the ever reached figure. With a 22 month window and a p25 of 21 months to Series A, only a minority of eventual raisers get there in time, so 0.26 times roughly 0.45 gives about 0.11. Voice AI peers have raised faster, so I do not go lower.

bands.rationale: Thin or small Series A, common for vertical software with early but modest revenue. Hot voice AI categories produced fast Series A rounds in 2024 and 2025, which supports the larger bands.
Central band around the 2022 and later Series A median of $15M (p25 $11M, p75 $21M).
Strong growth round led by a top tier fund.
Upside where the category is hot and revenue compounds fast.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series A needs enterprise contracts with real call volume, and call center buyers run long security reviews and pilots. Peers such as Retell AI (W24) and Bland AI (S23) had thousands of developer customers, while Calltree sells to enterprises and needs deep integrations. Inside the window it must turn pilots into multi year contracts, and a model vendor offering voice agents natively could undercut it.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2024 --industry B2B: series_b cond 21% (n=123), ever 3% known-only.
anchors.adjustment_reason: The anchor is the ever reached rate given Series A. A Series B inside a window of 22 months is rare because months_to_series_b has a median of 32 to 47 months from the batch start in time_to_milestones.csv, so only a breakout gets there.

bands.rationale: Thin Series B or bridge round of $10M to $20M, typical when growth is real but slower than the Series A story promised and investors want to see more revenue.
Central band; the 2022 and later Series B median is $40M.
Hot company band; the 2022 and later post money median is $600M.
Breakout upside above $70M at a valuation near $1B, reached only by the few companies that compound revenue quickly after a Series A.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series B inside the window would need an enterprise ramp to eight figure revenue, which almost no company of this kind does in under two years. Bland AI (S23) took years from batch to a Series B in the researched data, and Dataland (S20) shows the same slow path, so the window is too short for this step unless the company breaks out early.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2024 --industry B2B: series_c cond 19% (n=26), ever 1% known-only.
anchors.adjustment_reason: The anchor is conditional on Series B and ever reached, from a tiny sample. Inside the window almost nobody reaches Series C, so I keep a low nonzero figure for a breakout path with several fast rounds.

bands.rationale: Thin extension or flat round of $20M to $40M, used when a company needs more runway before it proves a Series C story.
Central band; the 2022 and later Series C median is $74M.
Strong growth round of $80M to $150M led by a growth fund, tied to a clear revenue ramp and category leadership.
Category leader upside above $150M at a multibillion valuation, seen only for the few companies that win a large market outright.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series C inside the window is close to impossible for a 14 person voice AI company, which would need several consecutive hypergrowth rounds. The researched Series C companies such as Postscript (W19) took roughly four to five years from batch, and nothing visible today points to the category defining ramp that would be required.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Most likely Calltree stalls or sells small: foundation model vendors and platforms such as Vapi and Synthflow commoditize voice agents, call center buyers keep humans for hard cases, and prices fall as every peer promises the same. Dataland (S20), an earlier customer support AI company, remains small, and Vogent (S21) was acquired.

analogs.outcome_summary: Active and fast growing; the closest peer with a stronger developer led growth channel.

Acquired; an exit path for infra style voice AI.

killers.risk: Voice AI platforms commoditize the product
killers.evidence: Vapi raised a $20M Series A in December 2024 and Synthflow raised $20M, and model vendors ship voice agents directly.
killers.mitigation: Compete on integrations with internal tools and measured resolution rates.

killers.risk: Enterprise sales cycles drain a 14 person team
killers.evidence: Call center operators run long pilots and security reviews, and pilots rarely convert inside a year.
killers.mitigation: Pick one vertical with high call volume and land one anchor customer.

killers.evidence: Public setbacks such as a fast food voice AI pilot pulled after errors show buyers will drop weak agents.
killers.mitigation: Show audited resolution accuracy and human handoff.

technical_complexity.rationale: Low latency voice, reliable tool use inside legacy internal dashboards and accuracy on live calls are hard; a small team can build a demo in three months but production quality with enterprise tools takes longer.

takeover_risk.rationale: Model vendors and contact center incumbents are adding voice agents, and tool use in a browser is now an agent feature, so copying is fast.

evidence.claim: Voice AI startups raised sharply more in 2024, with figures from $398M to $2.1B depending on the data source
Synthflow and Vapi raised $20M each, showing investor demand for enterprise voice agents

roadmap.goal: Show an agent resolving real enterprise calls with internal tools
actions: Run live calls for one call center
roadmap.proof: A paid pilot with named call volume

roadmap.goal: Convert pilots into contracts with named enterprises
Repeatable enterprise motion with integration library
actions: Build connectors to the top call center platforms
Hire enterprise sales and customer success
roadmap.proof: $2M annual recurring revenue with usage growth

pros.evidence: Vapi and Synthflow each raised $20M, showing capital for the category.
Using homegrown CRMs and dashboards is a harder buyer need than scripted bots, which may win enterprises with legacy stacks.

brand.name: Calltree
strengths: Call tree is a real call center term
weaknesses: Call tree is an existing phone menu term, hard to own in search
brand.rationale: Calltree reuses the phone menu term, which tells buyers what it does but is hard to own online. YC cases such as Bland AI (S23) show descriptive names sell in this field, so the name is neutral.

narrative.headline: A hot but crowded voice AI field; a priced seed inside 22 months is a little under even odds.
narrative.general_summary: Calltree sells enterprise voice and chat support agents that use internal tools. Investor appetite for voice AI is high, but Vapi, Synthflow and YC peers already raised and model vendors are moving in. Inside a 22 month window the seed probability follows the B2B timing curve, not a lift for the sector. A Series A inside the window is possible but less likely than not. The odds do not rank Calltree against other companies. The forecast window runs from the as of date to 2026-11-17, and later rounds are only counted if they close inside it.

assumptions: Only the input file was used about the company; no site, directory page or news about it was read.
Seed means a round above about $1M from outside investors, not the standard YC deal of about $500K, that closes inside the window.
The company is already in YC, so the acceptance figure is reported for completeness only.
Web search covered the market only. Results dated after the as of date or naming the company were to be ignored; none named it.
Funding coverage in the repo data is incomplete (see base_rates.py ranges), so the anchors are lower to upper ranges and not exact.
